correctness.rationale: Grossi–Moretti Theorem A establishes c2(X)=12, a Lagrangian Albanese immersion, one self-intersection pair. Their Lemma 6.1 itself explicitly gives [Z]^2=14 and the pulled-back class [W]=3([A x 0]+[0 x A])-[Delta]+H1H2 with W^2=126. Independently expanded the (1,6) NS intersection quartic 864(ab-c^2)^2: its fourth-degree monomial coefficients imply every integral product of two divisor classes on A x A squares to a multiple of 144. As 9[Z]^2=126 is not divisible by 144, a single integral Cartier divisor product on the quotient is impossible; no conclusion for rational combinations. This proves the statement but critically its inputs already come from the full published class calculation.
